title: Life Skills and Safety
description: Everyday skills that keep you safe and confident.

entries.title: Talking to Strangers
entries.summary: Be safe with people you do not know.
entries.body: A grown-up you trust should always know where you are. If a stranger asks you to keep a secret, that is a big red flag - tell an adult straight away. You can always say no, and you never have to feel rude about it.
facts: Never keep a secret from a grown-up you trust.
You do not have to go anywhere with someone who worries you.
If you feel unsafe, go to a place with other people.

entries.title: What To Do in a Fire
entries.summary: Get out fast and stay out.
entries.body: If there is a fire, get out of the building and go to a safe place, then call the fire service. Never hide under a bed or in a cupboard. Crawling low keeps you below the smoke, which is very dangerous.
facts: Get out and call the fire service.
Stay below the smoke - crawl low.
Never go back inside for belongings.

entries.title: Water Safety
entries.summary: Water can be dangerous if you are not careful.
entries.body: Never swim alone, always obey the flags at a beach, and always wear a life jacket on a boat. Drowning happens quietly and quickly, so stay close to an adult near water.
facts: Red and yellow flags mean the water is dangerous.
Wear a life jacket on a boat.

entries.title: Money
entries.summary: Money can be spent, saved or given.
entries.body: Money buys things and services. Some things you need, some you want, and some you can do without. Saving money means keeping it safe for something you really want later.
facts: Coins and notes are money; a debit card is also money.
It is smart to save for something you want.
Never share your PIN with anyone.

entries.title: Asking for Help
entries.summary: Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness.
entries.body: If something is too hard, if you are worried, or if you made a mistake, tell a grown-up or a teacher. Saying 'I need help with this' is something strong people do all the time.
facts: Adults expect to help - that is their job.
Telling someone early stops small problems becoming big ones.
It is fine to ask for help with something you find hard.

entries.title: Looking After Your Things
entries.body: Putting things away where they belong means you can find them later and nothing gets lost. Making your bed and packing your bag the night before makes a morning much calmer.
facts: Put things back where they belong.
Packing your bag the night before saves time in the morning.
Looking after your things means losing them less often.

questions.prompt: What should you do if a stranger asks you to keep a secret?
questions.explanation: Secrets from adults are a warning sign. Always tell someone you trust.

questions.prompt: What should you do in a fire?
options: Get out and call the fire service
questions.explanation: Get out fast, stay out, and call the fire service.

questions.prompt: When should you wear a life jacket?
questions.explanation: Always wear a life jacket on a boat.

questions.prompt: What should you do if a task feels too hard?
questions.explanation: Asking for help is a strong and sensible thing to do.
Drowning happens quickly and quietly, so stay near an adult.

questions.prompt: What is a good habit for the night before school?
questions.explanation: Packing the night before makes the morning much easier.

questions.prompt: Which is a safety rule on a beach?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow flags mean the water is dangerous.

questions.prompt: What should you never share with anyone?
questions.explanation: Never share your PIN or your passwords.

questions.prompt: What is the best thing to do with money you save?
options: Keep it for something you really want
questions.explanation: Saving means keeping it safe for later.
Putting things away means you can find them later.
